design_rationale: The study is described as a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial where patients were randomly assigned using a centralized computer-generated permuted-block sequence stratified by center via an interactive voice-response system.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation sequence was centrally computer-generated and concealed using an interactive voice-response system, with balanced baseline characteristics between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The random assignment list was computer-generated in permuted blocks of 4, stratified by center, by a clinical research organization (Covance, Radnor, Pennsylvania); staff obtained allocation assignments at the time of treatment by using a telephone interactive voice-response system.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study was double-blinded with identical-appearing placebo and analyzed appropriately according to allocated groups without substantial deviations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients who successfully completed open-label prophylaxis were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio in a double-blind manner to receive either subcutaneous enoxaparin, 40 mg/d, or placebo for an additional 28 ± 4 days... Patients, caregivers, and outcome assessors were blinded to group assignment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Nearly 18% of randomized participants lacked evaluable outcome data for the primary efficacy endpoint, which introduces some concerns despite sensitivity analyses and balanced proportions between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Approximately 18% (1090 of 6085) of all randomly assigned patients were unevaluable and were therefore excluded from the primary efficacy analysis... The unevaluable patients comprised 549 patients in the extended-duration enoxaparin group and 541 patients in the placebo group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome measurements were standardized and adjudicated by a central committee blinded to treatment assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In addition, all scans were centrally read by reviewers at Bio-Imaging Technologies (Newtown, Pennsylvania), who were blinded to treatment assignment, clinical information, and the local interpretation of the scan. Discrepancies between local and central readings were centrally adjudicated in blinded sessions...

domain_judgments.rationale: Eligibility criteria were amended mid-trial based on interim findings of lower-than-expected event rates, and post-hoc threshold definitions for safety endpoints were applied, raising some concerns regarding potential selection of reported results/analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Estimates of efficacy and safety for the overall trial population are difficult to interpret because of the change in eligibility criteria during the trial... The steering committee requested a blinded multivariate analysis on risk factors for VTE... The steering committee therefore issued a protocol amendment that changed the eligibility criteria to require patients with level 2 immobility to also have 1 or more of these risk factors...

overall_summary: The trial was well conducted and double-blinded with centralized allocation, but some concerns arise from the exclusion of ~18% of participants missing evaluable ultrasound outcome data and the mid-trial protocol amendment altering eligibility criteria after interim analysis.

design_rationale: The study is an open-label, multicentre, randomised controlled trial where participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to rivaroxaban or no anticoagulation using a central web-based randomisation system.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation sequence was generated centrally with concealed web-based automated randomization, and baseline characteristics were well-balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomisation was done in permuted blocks of variable size, using a central, concealed, web-based, automated randomisation system (RedCap, version 11.0.3).

domain_judgments.rationale: Although open-label, adherence was very high (99%), unintended deviations that arose from trial context were minimal, and an appropriate intention-to-treat approach was used.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The MICHELLE trial was an open-label study, with no masking of investigators or patients to group allocation... Eficacy analyses were done using the intention-to-treat principle. Two patients (one from each group) withdrew informed consent and were excluded from the primary analysis.

domain_judgments.rationale: There was substantial and differential missingness for the objective imaging components (CT pulmonary angiogram and bilateral lower limb Doppler ultrasound) comprising part of the primary composite outcome.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Not every patient received CT pulmonary angiogram (45 [28%] in the active group and 69 [43%] in the control group) or Doppler ultrasound (25 [16%] in the active group and 41 [26%] in the control group).

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome adjudication and imaging evaluations were conducted blindly by an independent committee and core laboratory according to standard objective criteria.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All events were evaluated by an independent clinical events adjudication committee, including a core laboratory for image analysis, whose members were unaware of the study treatment assignment.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary composite endpoint was amended during the study to include arterial thromboembolic events, and an interim analysis was conducted without formal stopping rules.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: During the study, we added an amendment including arterial events for the primary outcome... The statistical analysis plan was completed before the end of the study and unblinding of the study results and is available in the appendix (p 27).

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is judged to have some concerns due to substantial and differential missing screening imaging (CT angiograms and Doppler ultrasound) for the primary outcome components, as well as an in-trial amendment adding arterial events to the composite primary outcome.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive apixaban or enoxaparin via a central telephone system using a computer-generated randomization list.

domain_judgments.rationale: Central computer-generated randomization ensured appropriate sequence generation and allocation concealment, and baseline characteristics were well balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization was performed through a central telephone system with the use of a computer-generated randomization list.

domain_judgments.rationale: Double-blind, double-dummy design with placebo controls prevented awareness of assignment, and analyses followed the intended intervention protocols.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In this double-blind, double-dummy, placebo-controlled trial... The study medications were packaged in identical-appearing dispensing kits.

domain_judgments.rationale: Over 31% of randomized patients (2033 of 6528) were excluded from the primary efficacy analysis due to missing or unevaluable follow-up compression ultrasonography.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 6528 subjects underwent randomization, 4495 of whom could be evaluated for the primary efficacy outcome — 2211 in the apixaban group and 2284 in the enoxaparin group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were assessed with objective criteria and ultrasound examinations were centrally evaluated by an adjudication committee blinded to treatment assignments.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All components of the primary efficacy outcome were adjudicated by the independent central adjudication committee.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered, had an available pre-specified statistical analysis plan, and reported results in accordance with the planned analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study protocol, including the statistical analysis plan, is available with the full text of this article at NEJM.org... ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT00457002.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is high due to substantial missing outcome data (Domain 3), with approximately 31% of randomized participants excluded from the primary efficacy analysis because follow-up ultrasound examinations were missing or unevaluable.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated using permuted blocks via an interactive voice-response system to either rivaroxaban or enoxaparin.

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias arising from the randomization process
domain_judgments.rationale: Centralized interactive voice-response system ensured allocation concealment, and baseline characteristics were well-balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization was performed in permuted blocks with the use of an interactive voiceresponse system, with stratification according to center.

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias due to deviations from intended interventions
domain_judgments.rationale: The trial employed a double-dummy double-blind design with identical matching placebos, preventing awareness of assignment, and analyses adhered to prespecified modified intention-to-treat and per-protocol frameworks.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In this multicenter, randomized, double-blind trial, we evaluated the efficacy and safety of oral rivaroxaban administered for an extended period, as compared with subcutaneous enoxaparin administered for a standard period, followed by placebo.

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias due to missing outcome data
domain_judgments.rationale: Approximately 25% of randomized participants were excluded from the primary efficacy analyses at day 35 due to missing venous ultrasonography assessments, posing a high risk of bias given the low event rate (4.4% to 5.7%).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In the rivaroxaban group, an additional 765 patients were excluded from the modified intention-to-treat analysis at day 10 and 1030 at day 35, with the lack of an adequate assessment of venous thromboembolism as the main reason for exclusion. In the enoxaparin group, an additional 730 patients were excluded from the modified intention-to-treat analysis at day 10 and 944 at day 35.

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias in measurement of the outcome
domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were assessed by an independent, blinded central adjudication committee using objective diagnostic imaging protocols.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All outcomes were assessed by an independent, central adjudication committee whose members were unaware of the study assignments.

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias in selection of the reported result
domain_judgments.rationale: The trial followed a registered and published protocol (NCT00571649) with prespecified endpoints and analysis populations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The academic authors vouch for the accuracy and completeness of the report and for the fidelity of the report to the trial protocol, which is available at NEJM.org. ... The primary day 10 analysis was prespecified to be a noninferiority analysis, and the primary day 35 analysis was prespecified to be a superiority analysis.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high due to substantial missing outcome data (approximately 25% of patients lacked adequate venous thromboembolism assessments at day 35), which could meaningfully influence the primary efficacy findings.

design_rationale: The study was described as a randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled multinational trial using an interactive voice-response system to assign participants to study groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: Randomization used permuted blocks stratified by relevant factors and centralized allocation concealment via an interactive voice-response system, with balanced baseline characteristics between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We used permuted blocks to stratify eligible patients... An interactive voice-response system was used to randomly assign patients to receive one of two regimens

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was double-blind and double-dummy with active controls, minimizing deviations from intended interventions, and analyzed using appropriate modified intention-to-treat frameworks.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The APEX trial was a randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, active-controlled, multinational clinical trial.

domain_judgments.rationale: A substantial proportion of randomized patients (15.4%) were excluded from the primary efficacy outcome analysis due to missing ultrasonography, though missingness was balanced across groups and sensitivity imputation yielded similar results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: ...and 1155 patients (15.4% of those who underwent randomization) were excluded from the efficacy analyses because they did not have a symptomatic event associated with venous thromboembolism and did not undergo ultrasonography between day 32 and day 47.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessors and the central end-point adjudication committee were blinded to treatment allocation, and objective diagnostic criteria were applied across both groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All outcomes were assessed by an independent, central end-point adjudication committee whose members were unaware of treatment assignments.

domain_judgments.rationale: The outcomes and hierarchical testing strategy were prespecified in a published protocol/statistical analysis plan, and reported results follow this prespecified sequence transparently.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Plans for the statistical analysis have been reported previously and are available at NEJM.org. The three cohorts that were included in the efficacy analysis were prespecified in a procedure with a fixed hierarchical sequence to adjust for the type I error rate.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns, driven primarily by the missing outcome data domain where approximately 15% of participants lacked day 32-47 ultrasonography data and were excluded from the primary efficacy analysis.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to rivaroxaban or placebo using an interactive Web-based system with permuted blocks.

domain_judgments.rationale: Randomization was centrally managed via an interactive Web-based system using permuted blocks, ensuring allocation concealment, and baseline characteristics were well balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive either rivaroxaban or placebo. Randomization was performed on the day of discharge from the hospital or the next day, with the use of an interactive Web-based system, with stratification according to country and creatinine clearance (≥30 and <50 ml per minute or ≥50 ml per minute). Randomization was balanced in permuted blocks of four.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was double-blinded with placebo control, blinding was maintained, and the primary efficacy analysis followed an intention-to-treat approach including essentially all randomized patients.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In this randomized, double-blind trial... All the efficacy analyses were performed with the intention-to-treat population and included all data and outcomes from randomization through day 45.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for 12,019 out of 12,024 randomized patients (>99.9%), demonstrating negligible missing outcome data.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of the 12,024 patients who underwent randomization, 12,019 were included in the intention-to-treat analysis.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were assessed with prespecified criteria and evaluated by an independent clinical events committee whose members were blinded to trial-group assignments.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A clinical events committee, the members of which were unaware of the trial-group assignments, adjudicated all suspected episodes of venous thromboembolism, bleeding, myocardial infarction, and stroke and all deaths, with the use of prespecified criteria.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study protocol and statistical analysis plan were prespecified and registered, and all prespecified primary and secondary outcomes were reported in accordance with the pre-established hierarchical plan.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The trial was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT02111564), and the primary and secondary outcomes, statistical analyses, and hierarchical testing procedure were prespecified in published protocol and statistical analysis plans.

overall_summary: The study was a rigorously conducted, large double-blind randomized controlled trial with central allocation concealment, blinding of participants and outcome adjudicators, negligible missing data, and full adherence to a prespecified analysis protocol. Therefore, the overall risk of bias is judged to be low across all domains.

design_rationale: The study is described as a randomized open-label trial in which 300 consecutive medical patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to two thromboprophylaxis duration groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: While the study states patients were randomized 1:1, there is no information provided regarding the sequence generation method or allocation concealment, and some baseline imbalances were noted (smoking and dehydration).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 300 consecutive medical patients (155 M, 145 F, mean age, 67.8 ±4 years) were randomly assigned in an open-label study to two groups (1:1). ... In stage 1 the patients where randomized in one of the two groups (I, II) 1:1.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although the study was open-label, the intervention duration was strictly protocolized, all assigned participants received their intended duration, and there were no reported dropouts or deviations affecting the intervention delivery.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: During prophylactic treatment no patient dropped out of the study nor any death occurred. ... In group I nadroparin prophylactic treatment was administered only during patient immobilization, in group II during immobilization and for following 10 days.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data appear to be completely reported for all 300 randomized participants across both groups during the 3-month follow-up.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: During a further 3-month follow-up of all the 300 patients, death of unknown causes or deep-vein thrombosis were found in 17 (5.6%) patients, including 2 patients who suddenly died.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study was open-label and there is no mention of blinding of the ultrasound operators or assessors evaluating the compression ultrasound test for deep vein thrombosis, which involves subjective diagnostic interpretation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: For confirmation or exclusion of deep vein thrombosis an ultrasound compression test in four points (with the use of the GE LOGIQ 200 PRO machine, and a 6–9 MHz linear probe) was performed three times in each patient: on the day of admision, upon completion of prophylactic treatment, and upon completion of a 3-month follow-up.

domain_judgments.rationale: No pre-registration or published statistical analysis protocol is cited, leaving some concern regarding the potential for selective reporting of outcomes and analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Lower extremity deep-vein thrombosis confirmed by a four point ultrasound compression test, upon completion of prophylactic treatment or during a 3-month follow-up, or death regardless of its reason, were considered end points. Adverse effects of nadroparin, especially hemorrhagic complications were assessed.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns due to lack of reporting on allocation concealment and random sequence generation details, lack of blinded outcome assessment for compression ultrasonography in an open-label trial, and absence of a pre-registered analysis plan.
